principles: Each AI tool's home directory has exactly ONE owner.
No tool may auto-discover, auto-spawn, or auto-register from another tool's directory without explicit allowlist entry.
Cross-tool reads are allowed only when the reader is named in readers_allowed for that path.
Every protected directory carries a .no-auto-discovery sentinel as a low-cost signal to well-behaved tools (and a tripwire for the daily sentinel scan).

~/.claude/.notes: User-level Claude Code config: skills, hooks, commands, plugins, projects/ (transcripts!), memory.

~/.claude/plugins/.notes: Apr 26-29 2026: Cursor's anysphere.cursor-mcp extension auto-scanned this dir, registered every plugin as a Cursor MCP server, and stacked 6 zombie bridge processes racing OpenClaw for the asterix Discord gateway. NEVER allow another tool to read this path.

~/.claude/projects/.notes: Session transcripts live here. Contains historical secret leaks (per ROTATION-MAP.md). Treat as sensitive.

~/.openclaw/.notes: MC reads observability files only. MC may NEVER write here.

~/.openclaw/token-claims/.notes: flock-managed lockfiles. MC referees but does not claim.

~/.codex/.notes: Session jsonl files contain historical secret leaks (~20 INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET hits per ROTATION-MAP.md). Sensitive.

~/.hermes/.host_note: Lives on m1book primarily. Mac-side may have a thin client config only.

~/.cursor/.notes: Cursor's built-in cursor-mcp extension was quarantined 2026-04-29 to ~/security-incident-2026-04-29/quarantine-cursor-mcp/cursor-mcp-app-bundle/. Cursor app updates will reinstall it — see daily_sentinel checks below.

/Applications/Cursor.app/Contents/Resour.notes: Cursor's auto-discovery feature lives here. App updates restore it. A launchd watch on this path is the right enforcement.

sentinel.contents: This directory is owned by a single tool. Other AI tools must NOT auto-discover, auto-register, or spawn processes from contents here. See ~/projects/config/namespace-ownership.policy.json.

daily_sentinel_checks._replaced_by_below_2026-05-04: Original `awk '$1 != "node"'` whitelist was too broad — it allowed BOTH legitimate Claude plugin runtime AND the actual Cursor bridges (which are commonly Node/bun processes). Replaced with parent-process-aware checks below per courtroom verdict 2026-05-04 (Codex objection #5, severity major).

daily_sentinel_checks._comment: Replacement for the over-broad node-name whitelist. Enumerate every PID with a fd inside ~/.claude/plugins via lsof, walk up to the parent process, and FAIL on any parent comm not in the allowlist. Allowlist: claude, claude-code (Claude Code runtime); reject explicitly: Cursor, Cursor Helper (Plugin), Code, Code Helper (Plugin), bun (when its parent isn't claude). The ppid lookup is the load-bearing piece — process name alone collides between Claude's and Cursor's runtimes.
daily_sentinel_checks.command: set -o pipefail; ALLOW='^(claude|claude-code|node)$'; PARENT_ALLOW='^(claude|claude-code|launchd)$'; bad=$(lsof -nFpcR +D ~/.claude/plugins 2>/dev/null | awk 'BEGIN{p="";c="";r=""} /^p/{if(p!="")print p"|"c"|"r; p=substr($0,2); c=""; r=""} /^c/{c=substr($0,2)} /^R/{r=substr($0,2)} END{if(p!="")print p"|"c"|"r}' | while IFS='|' read pid comm ppid; do echo "$comm" | grep -Eq "$ALLOW" || { echo "NAME-NOT-ALLOWED: $pid $comm (ppid=$ppid)"; continue; }; pcomm=$(ps -o comm= -p "$ppid" 2>/dev/null | xargs basename 2>/dev/null); echo "$pcomm" | grep -Eq "$PARENT_ALLOW" || echo "PARENT-NOT-ALLOWED: $pid $comm parent=$pcomm"; done); test -z "$bad"
daily_sentinel_checks.on_fail: alert with the bad-process list AND the relevant `ps -ef` rows for the offending ppids — operator needs both pieces to identify the foreign tool
_known_offenders_to_catch: Cursor's anysphere.cursor-mcp extension spawning under 'Cursor Helper (Plugin)' parent
bun run --cwd ~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/discord/* with parent NOT in claude-code

daily_sentinel_checks._comment: Belt-and-suspenders for the specific Cursor bridge cmdline shape from project_discord_bridge_zombie_launchers memory. If a `bun` process has its working dir inside ~/.claude/plugins AND its parent isn't a claude-code process, alert and kill.
daily_sentinel_checks.command: set -o pipefail; bad=$(pgrep -fl 'bun.*--cwd.*\.claude/plugins' 2>/dev/null | while read pid rest; do ppid=$(ps -o ppid= -p "$pid" | tr -d ' '); pcomm=$(ps -o comm= -p "$ppid" 2>/dev/null | xargs basename 2>/dev/null); case "$pcomm" in claude|claude-code) ;; *) echo "$pid $rest (parent=$pcomm)";; esac; done); test -z "$bad"
daily_sentinel_checks.on_fail: alert + offer kill of matching PIDs (do NOT auto-kill — parent might be legitimate user-launched debug session)
